{{nihongo|'''Homi Shrine (Asahimachi, Nirasaki)'''|穂見神社}} is a shrine in Kamijō Minamiwari, Asahi-chō, {{ill|Nirasaki, Yamanashi|Q290326|qid=Q290326}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|Q132720|qid=Q132720}}. It is a candidate shrine for a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} and was formerly a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. Also called Nadeshikiyama Gongen. {{nihongo|'''Homi Shrine (Asahimachi, Nirasaki)'''|穂見神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kai Province]].
The {{ill|Saijin|abstract|Q11591100|fr|Saijin|ja|祭神|zh|祭神|qid=Q11591100}} are {{ill|Ame-no-Tokotachi|Q10939047|qid=Q10939047|lt=Ame-no-Sokotachi-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Kuni-no-Tokotachi|lt=Kunitokotachi-no-Kami|Q478504|qid=Q478504|lt=Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Q2983724|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke-hime-no-Mikoto}}.

==History==
[[File:Homi_Shrine_Torii.JPG|thumb|220px|<center>Torii</center>]]
The {{ill|hongū|Q11520115|qid=Q11520115}} (okumiya) is near the summit of Nadeshiki-yama (Asahi-yama), elevation 1037 m, and the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=satomiya}} is on the eastern foot of the mountain. The satomiya area, Kamijō Minamiwari of Nirasaki Asahi-chō, lies on the western edge of the {{ill|Kōfu Basin|Q11577819|qid=Q11577819}}, on a terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamanashi River}}, with the {{ill|Midai River|Q11488828|qid=Q11488828}} flowing south.

This area in medieval times belonged to {{ill|Amari-shō|Q11574250|qid=Q11574250}}, and in early modern times Kamijō Minamiwari village was established. Nadeshiki-yama is 1032 m high and is said to have prospered as a mountain of faith in the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}.

The {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}} deity register records “Homi Shrine” in Koma District. Candidate shrines include this shrine, {{ill|Homi Shrine|ja|穂見神社|qid=Q11597094|lt=Homi Shrine}} in Anayama-chō, Nirasaki, and {{ill|Homi Shrine|ja|穂見神社 (南アルプス市)|qid=Q11597095|lt=Homi Shrine}} in Takao, {{ill|Minami-Alps, Yamanashi|Q824000|qid=Q824000}}. Formerly called Nadeshikiyama Gongen, and on the summit there is said to have been the {{ill|Shingon Buddhism|Q550182|qid=Q550182}} temple Nadeshikiyama Hōshō-ji (now abandoned) as {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}}. Remains of the mountain gate, guardian gate, bell tower, and foundations/terraces of guest hall and kitchen have been confirmed, along with excavated artifacts such as {{ill|Haji pottery|Q5639938|qid=Q5639938}}, {{ill|ink-inscribed pottery|ja|墨書土器|qid=Q11429419}}, and {{ill|green-glazed pottery|ja|緑釉陶器|qid=Q48758368}}.

According to ''{{ill|Kaikokushi|Q11577871|qid=Q11577871}}'', it once had a vast sacred precinct but declined after military damage in the {{ill|Tenshō-Jingo war|fa|درگیری تنشو-جینگو|it|Conflitto Tenshō-Jingo|ja|天正壬午の乱|ko|덴쇼 진고의 난|zh|天正壬午之亂|qid=Q10939819}}. In the Sengoku period it was protected by the Kai shugo {{ill|Takeda clan|Q1210114|qid=Q1210114}}; according to ''Kai no Kuni Shaki/Jiki'', in {{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}} 9 ({{ill|1566|ab|1566|af|1566|als|1566|am|1566 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1566|ar|1566|ary|1566|arz|1566|ast|1566|avk|1566|az|1566|azb|۱۵۶۶ (میلادی)|bar|1566|bcl|1566|be|1566|be_x_old|1566|bg|1566|bn|১৫৬৬|bpy|মারি ১৫৬৬|br|1566|bs|1566.|ca|1566|cdo|1566 nièng|ce|1566 шо|ceb|1566|ckb|١٥٦٦|crh|1566|cs|1566|cv|1566|cy|1566|da|1566|de|1566|diq|1566|el|1566|eml|1566|eo|1566|es|1566|et|1566|eu|1566|fa|۱۵۶۶ (میلادی)|fi|1566|fo|1566|fr|1566|frr|1566|fur|1566|fy|1566|ga|1566|gan|1566年|gcr|1566|gd|1566|gl|1566|gv|1566|he|1566|hi|१५६६|hr|1566.|ht|1566 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1566|hy|1566|ia|1566|id|1566|ilo|1566|io|1566|is|1566|it|1566|ja|1566年|jv|1566|ka|1566|kaa|1566|kk|1566 жыл|ko|1566년|krc|1566 джыл|ku|1566|la|1566|lb|1566|lij|1566|lmo|1566|lt|1566 m.|lv|1566. gads|mai|१५६६|map_bms|1566|mdf|1566|mg|1566|mhr|1566|mi|1566|min|1566|mk|1566|mr|इ.स. १५६६|mrj|1566 и|ms|1566|my|၁၅၆၆|mzn|۱۵۶۶|nah|1566|nap|1566|nds|1566|new|सन् १५६६|nl|1566|nn|1566|no|1566|nrm|1566|nso|1566|oc|1566|or|୧୫୬୬|os|1566-æм аз|pl|1566|pnb|1566|pt|1566|qu|1566|ro|1566|ru|1566 год|rue|1566|sa|१५६६|sah|1566|scn|1566|sd|1566ع|se|1566|sh|1566.|shn|1566|simple|1566|sk|1566|sl|1566|smn|1566|sq|1566|sr|1566|su|1566|sv|1566|sw|1566|ta|1566|te|1566|tg|Соли 1566|th|พ.ศ. 2109|tk|1566|tl|1566|tly|1566|tr|1566|tt|1566 ел|uk|1566|ur|1566ء|uz|1566|vec|1566|vi|1566|vls|1566|wa|1566|war|1566|wuu|1566年|xmf|1566|yi|1566|zh|1566年|zh_min_nan|1566 nî|zh_yue|1566年|qid=Q6638}}) it was exempted from munabetsu tax and construction labor. In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 13 (1583), {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}} confirmed its shrine lands.

In the early modern period, several halls stood in the precincts, including Kokūzō Hall enshrining {{ill|Ākāśagarbha|Q416174|qid=Q416174}}, the shrine’s honji-butsu. Kokūzō Bosatsu is linked to lake traditions of the Kōfu Basin and to a creation legend that opened the basin, planted seedlings, and taught rice cultivation; worshippers came to pray for crop abundance. The mountain name “Nadeshiki-yama” derives from this creation legend.

Along the approach to the okumiya are chō-seki markers set in {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 4 ({{ill|1691|Q7682|qid=Q7682}}), and at the 13-chō point stands a stone torii from {{ill|Kanbun (era)|es|Kanbun|fa|کانبون (دوره)|fr|Ère Kanbun|id|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|ko|간분|ru|Камбун (нэнго)|simple|Kanbun (era)|sr|Канбун (ера)|sv|Kanbun|tr|Kanbun (dönem)|zh|寬文|qid=Q1146228}} 4 ({{ill|1664|ab|1664|af|1664|als|1664|am|1664 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1664|ar|1664|ary|1664|arz|1664|ast|1664|avk|1664|az|1664|azb|۱۶۶۴ (میلادی)|ban|1664|bcl|1664|be|1664|be_x_old|1664|bg|1664|bn|১৬৬৪|bpy|মারি ১৬৬৪|br|1664|bs|1664.|ca|1664|cdo|1664 nièng|ceb|1664|ckb|١٦٦٤|crh|1664|cs|1664|cv|1664|cy|1664|da|1664|de|1664|diq|1664|el|1664|eml|1664|eo|1664|es|1664|et|1664|eu|1664|fa|۱۶۶۴ (میلادی)|fi|1664|fo|1664|fr|1664|frp|1664|frr|1664|fur|1664|fy|1664|ga|1664|gan|1664年|gcr|1664|gd|1664|gl|1664|gv|1664|he|1664|hi|१६६४|hr|1664.|hsb|1664|ht|1664 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1664|hy|1664|hyw|1664 թուական|ia|1664|id|1664|ilo|1664|io|1664|is|1664|it|1664|ja|1664年|jv|1664|ka|1664|kaa|1664|kk|1664 жыл|ko|1664년|krc|1664 джыл|la|1664|lb|1664|lij|1664|lmo|1664|lt|1664 m.|lv|1664. gads|mai|१६६४|map_bms|1664|mdf|1664|mg|1664|mhr|1664|mi|1664|mk|1664|mr|इ.स. १६६४|mrj|1664 и|ms|1664|my|၁၆၆၄|myv|1664 ие|mzn|۱۶۶۴|nah|1664|nap|1664|nds|1664|new|सन् १६६४|nl|1664|nn|1664|no|1664|nov|1664|nrm|1664|nso|1664|oc|1664|or|୧୬୬୪|os|1664-æм аз|pa|1664|pl|1664|pnb|1664|pt|1664|qu|1664|ro|1664|ru|1664 год|rue|1664|sa|१६६४|sah|1664|scn|1664|sd|1664ع|se|1664|sh|1664.|shn|1664|simple|1664|sk|1664|sl|1664|smn|1664|sq|1664|sr|1664|stq|1664|su|1664|sv|1664|sw|1664|szl|1664|ta|1664|te|1664|tg|Соли 1664|th|พ.ศ. 2207|tk|1664|tl|1664|tly|1664|tr|1664|tt|1664 ел|uk|1664|ur|1664ء|uz|1664|vec|1664|vi|1664|vls|1664|wa|1664|war|1664|wuu|1664年|xmf|1664|yi|1664|zh|1664年|zh_classical|一六六四年|zh_min_nan|1664 nî|zh_yue|1664年|qid=Q7581}}). The approach has repeatedly deteriorated and been rerouted over time; later excavations could not locate many markers, especially continuously from 4-chō to 18-chō. The stone torii at 13-chō is now slightly off the present path, and clear traces before and after it are lacking, so the old route through the torii is not well understood.

{{ill|Hagiwara Motoe|ja|萩原元克|qid=Q6537296}}’s ''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kai Meishōshi}}'' transmits a waka by {{ill|Saigyō|ar|ساتو نوريكيو|arz|ساتو نوريكيو|bcl|Saigyo|cs|Saigjó|de|Saigyō|es|Saigyō|et|Saigyō|fa|سایگیو|fi|Saigyō|fr|Saigyō Hōshi|hu|Szaigjó Hósi|it|Saigyō|ja|西行|ko|사이교|pl|Saigyō|ru|Сайгё|sh|Saigyo|tr|Saigyō|uk|Сайґьо|zh|西行|zh_classical|西行|zh_yue|西行|qid=Q224689}} on the view from Nadeshiki-yama, but ''Kai no Kuni Shi'' rejects it as lacking firm evidence.
[[ファイル:十三丁目の石鳥居.jpg|サムネイル|Stone torii at 13-chō on the Nadeshikiyama okumiya approach]]
In 2001, remains from ancient to medieval periods were found during forest-road construction near the summit. This led to three academic excavations; especially in the third, large-scale surveys covered the approach from satomiya to okumiya and the summit area. Across the three surveys, Heian-period Haji ware, hearth traces, and pit-house remains were found, showing that rituals were already being conducted around the time of formation of Amari-shō at the mountain foot. However, even these surveys did not newly find remains or artifacts from the 13th-15th centuries (Kamakura-Muromachi), so the condition of the Nadeshiki-yama area including Homi Shrine okumiya in that period remains unclear. Results were compiled in the 2011 ''Comprehensive Academic Survey Report on Nadeshiki-yama''.

== Access to the okumiya ==
From satomiya to okumiya is about 1.5-2 hours one way on foot. Most of the present route is unpaved forest road, with part as mountain trail, so mountaineering-level equipment is recommended.
